result:
Not every screen reached a 4. The critic scored 18 and 25 at 3 and the Display settings screen (72) at 2. The pad-buttons screen (74) stayed at 2 in the last runs I did. I stopped after two follow-up ships that didn't raise the scores. Screens 75 (pad rebind) and 26, 32, 42 and 49 were last scored at 2 or 3, before this run's changes, and I didn't re-run them.

27–31, 68–71 and 73 were never scored separately. They use the same shell as 72 and 74, so I didn't spend critic runs on them.

Two changes shipped this run, both through the gate and passing preflight:
- **v30.13, `cw-sethint`:** the Settings and Keys cards now end in one key-hint line. It reads "Esc Close" on a keyboard, and on a pad "LB RB Tabs", "A Change" and "B Back". The backdrop is 98% void with a 14px blur, so no menu text shows through.
- **v30.15, `cw-sethint2`:** the hint is 20px. The list fade is 24px instead of 32 with 24px of padding under the last row, and pad rows have 8px of air above and below.

The critic called the pad-buttons result "same" as before, and the pause box also came back "same". On the Display screen (72) it said "better, but still a 2".

It is also contradicting itself. It asks for the world dimmed to about 55% and for the HUD hidden. It complains about ghost text behind the card, then calls the darker backdrop a loss. Findings I left alone:
- **Focus row:** the staged shots have no pad cursor, so "no focus state" repeats. Real play does show a raised fill and an amber bar.
- **Wording:** the pad labels that wrap to three lines, and the "Edit the words" help line, are his wording.
- **Pause box:** the critic wants Feedback and What's new turned into list rows and Abandon turned into a link. That would move his buttons, so I didn't.

The rest is logged in `notes/c-31-ui-pause-settings.md` and one line in `notes/ui/changes.md`. The next step there is real keycap elements for the hints, pad glyphs, and a staging with a pad cursor for screens 26 and 74.

TASK PARTIAL: critic scores are still 2–3 on 18, 25, 72, 74 and 75; the remaining findings need keycap elements, pad glyphs and a pad-focus staging, or reverse his wording.
